basis: Familial dwarfism with painful muscle spasms defines skeletal and muscle involvement; no evidence establishes an endocrine or neurologic disorder.
Axial skeletal mineralization disorder; renal and hepatic cyst annotations lack frequencies sufficient to establish common involvement.
Nonsyndromic partial cataract affects the ocular lens.
Senior-Loken syndrome is defined by nephronophthisis and retinal dystrophy; kidney failure 21/21 and rod-cone dystrophy 7/21.
Acquired deficiency anemia is a blood-cell disorder; additional organ damage is not uniform across this group.
Immune-mediated necrotizing GN with small-vessel vasculitis in 80–99%; broad skin/respiratory annotations do not establish common damaging lesions.
Immune-mediated cerebellar dysfunction defines both the neurologic location and immune mechanism.
Choroidal atrophy and ectodermal hair/nail abnormalities define the syndrome; middle-ear disease is occasional.
Viral infection umbrella encompassing different tissue tropisms; no single damaged organ is established across the group.
Tumor originates in the Bartholin gland, a reproductive accessory gland outside the organ axes.
Gonadal and sex-development disorder encompassing abnormalities of sex-hormone production or action; no consistent additional organ damage.
Atherosclerotic thrombotic occlusion of the abdominal aorta; claudication alone does not establish separate muscle damage.
Microcephaly and severe axonal neuropathy define the syndrome; progressive muscle wasting and scoliosis are characteristic common structural consequences.
Inherited high myopia affects the eye; retinal detachment remains within the same axis.
Structural malformation of the cerebellum and brainstem; associated hydrocephalus is also neurologic.
Heterogeneous viral infections; myocarditis, meningitis and other organ-specific syndromes do not characterize most infections.
Benign neoplasm originating in the cerebellum.
Inflammation of the parotid salivary gland; infection or autoimmunity is not required by the umbrella definition.
Immunodeficiency with dermatitis in 8/8; asthma (5/8) and pneumonia (4/8) are separate diseases; bronchiectasis occurs in only 1/8.
Developmental epileptic encephalopathy; cerebral visual impairment is neurologic, without evidence of intrinsic eye damage.
Glyoxalase II deficiency is an inherited metabolic enzyme defect; no common organ damage beyond the metabolic abnormality is established.
Prenatal destructive brain injury defines fetal brain disruption sequence.
Astrocytic CNS tumor; an IDH mutation does not itself establish a systemic metabolic disorder.
Benign eccrine sweat-gland neoplasm arising in the dermis.
Keloids represent excessive fibrous scar formation in the skin.
